pr_body:
Added ESQL function to get the prefix of an IP.
It works now with both IPv4 and IPv6. For users planning to use it with mixed IPs, we may need to add a function like "is_ipv4()" first.

**About the skipped test:** There's currently a "bug" in the evaluators//functions that return null. Evaluators can't handle them. We'll work on support for that in another PR.
It affects other functions, like `substring()`. In this function, however, it only affects in "wrong" cases (Like an invalid prefix), so it has no impact.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/99064

issue_context.title: IP aggregation by CIDR length
issue_context.body:
### Description

We store a lot of network related data in ES - firewall hits, proxy logs, syslog etc., a lot of times I find the need to aggregate the results into subnets.  I can do this by manually defining IP buckets for the results to go into, but if i want to group the results by say /24 ranges, I would need to build an awful lot of buckets to do this - more than is probably possible, and the results would only populate a small number of buckets.

It would be great to define a CIDR aggregation type with the prefix length being the only required value, and the resulting aggregated values being bucketed by CIDR range.

We use a cloud data app that does something similar to this, see attached images

![cidr-picker](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/assets/12939628/11631f1e-a2d2-49b9-a704-ef2c5b52e55c)


![cidr-results](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/assets/12939628/119e414e-6240-4748-bfce-867dc9b140e7)
comments:
Apologies for the late reply.

@jammib Does the [`ip_prefix` aggregation](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/8.11/search-aggregations-bucket-ipprefix-aggregation.html) do what is requested here?  I think using this aggregation with a `prefix_length` of 24 would what you describe?

review_comments: If you do `@Evaluator(warnExceptions= IllegalArgumentException)` then these will turn into a warning and a `null` value which seems nice. Better than aborting the query with an exception.
What's up here? I'd figured `split` defaulted to as many strings as there are `-`s

Actually, we're probably moving away from these in favor of those capabilities anyway. Or features. I forget which one. The REST layer one. Either way, I think we're not using the version skipping much any more.

Quite obscure, but the 2 params form of split keeps the empty strings.

`"-".split("-") == []`
`"a-".split("-") == ["a"]`
`"-".split("-", 123) == ["", ""]`
`"a-".split("-", 123) == ["a", ""]`

Changed this as it was _convenient_ for my PR (Skipping that null test), while it still looked like the expected behaviour of that function (It already handles an empty upper bound)

I *think* you don't need `@FunctionName` here - we guess the function name using heuristics from the class name. And if we can't do `PascalCase` then we should fix that. There's some method in some string utility class to do that conversion somewhere....
